**DK25.6** is a medical diagnosis code used in the Danish healthcare system to classify a chronic or unspecified gastric ulcer accompanied by both bleeding and perforation [^src1] [^src2] [^src3]. Within the context of the national clinical quality database for [[atrieflimren]], managed by the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP), this code plays a specific role in monitoring patient safety and treatment complications.

Specifically, DK25.6 is utilized as part of the clinical indicator measuring the incidence of [[alvorlig-bloedning|Alvorlig blødning]] among patients diagnosed with atrial fibrillation [^src1] [^src3]. Because patients with atrial fibrillation are frequently treated with anticoagulants, they are at an elevated risk for severe bleeding events. To accurately capture these events in national registries, the methodology employs a broad spectrum of ICD-10 diagnosis codes. 

For gastrointestinal bleeding, the tracking encompasses codes ranging from DK25.0 to DK29.8A and DK92.0 to DK92.2 [^src1]. DK25.6 sits within this gastrointestinal category, specifically flagging one of the most critical and life-threatening ulcer complications—simultaneous bleeding and perforation [^src1] [^src2] [^src3]. This rigorous coding methodology allows Danish health authorities to systematically monitor and compare the quality of care and the rate of severe adverse events across different regions over time.

## Claims
